contexts.title: Recruiter brief - Senior Firmware Engineer, Motor Control
contexts.text:
RECRUITER BRIEF - Senior Firmware Engineer, Motor Control
Fernhollow Robotics | Req FR-2291 | Owner: recruiter Ines Calderwood | Updated Sep 25

THE ROLE
Fernhollow builds autonomous mowers for golf courses and municipal parks. This hire joins the Motion Controls team and owns the brushless motor drive firmware on the M4 mower platform: current loops, field-oriented control, fault handling, and bring-up of the next motor controller board.

TEAM
Motion Controls is 7 firmware engineers plus a hardware liaison, led by engineering manager Keziah Adebayo-Lund. The team sits inside a 60-person robotics org.

MUST-HAVES
- 6+ years writing production embedded C.
- Hands-on field-oriented control (FOC) for BLDC or PMSM motors, including tuning current loops on real hardware.
- RTOS experience (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or similar).
- Comfortable with a scope and a logic analyzer.

NICE-TO-HAVES
- Functional safety work (IEC 61508 or ISO 13849).
- Rust on microcontrollers.
- Outdoor or agricultural equipment experience.

WHERE AND HOW
Hybrid. Two anchor days in the Fremont lab, Tuesday and Wednesday, because the dynamometers and prototype boards live there. The other three days are flexible. Fully remote is not available for this role.

BENEFITS HIGHLIGHTS (share freely)
- Parental leave: 16 weeks fully paid for all parents, plus a 4-week phased return at a reduced schedule with full pay.
- 20 days PTO plus a winter shutdown week.
- 401(k) with a 5% match.
- Sign-on bonus: up to $15,000, approved case by case by the VP of Engineering.
- $1,500 yearly learning budget.

INTERVIEW STEPS
1. Recruiter screen, 30 minutes (this call).
2. Hiring manager call with Keziah, 45 minutes.
3. Onsite at Fremont, about 4 hours: an embedded C session, a control-theory whiteboard session, and a hardware debugging lab on a live motor rig, followed by lunch with the team.
4. Decision within 5 business days of the onsite. References only after a verbal offer.

COMPENSATION
Do not quote a range on the screen. The band is shared after the hiring manager call, once leveling is clear.

SELLING POINTS
- Real hardware that ships every season; firmware changes reach about 2,000 mowers in the field.
- The team rebuilt its CI so every merge is flashed onto hardware-in-the-loop rigs overnight.
- Low meeting load: one team meeting a week.

SOURCING NOTES (internal, do not share)
- Two candidates declined over the anchor days last month.
- Keziah prefers people who can talk through a failure they debugged on hardware.
- Do not discuss the Q3 reorg of the autonomy group.

contexts.title: Intake notes - Req 4471 Data Engineer II
contexts.text:
INTAKE NOTES - Req 4471, Data Engineer II (updated after sync with hiring manager)
Company: Tanglewood Mutual Insurance | Recruiter: Obi Hartmann | Hiring manager: Delphine Sorensen

HEADLINE
Location: Remote (US). Target start: January 12. Team of 5.

FROM THE INTAKE CALL (Sep 10)
- Joins the claims data team, which owns the pipelines feeding the fraud models and the actuarial warehouse.
- Stack: dbt, Airflow, Snowflake, a few Python services.
- Delphine wants someone who has owned a migration end to end, not just contributed to one.
- Nice to have: insurance or claims domain knowledge. Not required.

UPDATES FROM HM SYNC (Sep 26)
- Delphine now needs someone in seat before the Dec 1 platform freeze so they can shadow the Snowflake cutover. Her words: 'January is too late.'
- After the merge with the pricing analytics group, the new hire joins a combined team of 9.
- Leadership wants data engineers in the Austin office 3 days a week starting next quarter. Remote exceptions need VP sign-off.

INTERVIEW LOOP
Four rounds: recruiter screen, SQL and modeling exercise, pipeline design with two engineers.

COMP
Band: $128,000 - $150,000 base. Later note: band under review after the merge, do not share until confirmed.

OTHER
- Visa: case by case, check with HR before promising anything.
- Candidates keep asking about on-call: one week in eight, business hours only.
- Benefits deck is the 2025 version; HR says the 2026 one lands in November.
- Headline section has not been updated since the intake call.
contexts.notes: Contradictions: target start January 12 (headline) vs in seat before the Dec 1 platform freeze (HM sync); Remote (US) (headline) vs Austin office 3 days a week (HM sync); team of 5 (headline) vs combined team of 9 (HM sync); loop says four rounds but lists three; band is written down but then marked do-not-share.

RECRUITING TEAM - Q4 OFFSITE AGENDA
Thursday Oct 23, Lakeview room, 9:30 to 3:30

9:30  Coffee and a quick round of wins from Q3
10:00 Pipeline review by function (engineering, sales, operations). Bring your top three stuck reqs.
11:00 Sourcing experiment readout: the referral bonus bump did not move referral volume; the alumni newsletter did, slightly.
11:45 Calibration exercise: everyone scores the same three anonymized phone-screen notes, then we compare.
12:30 Lunch (tacos; tell Rosalind about dietary needs by Monday)
1:30  ATS cleanup: closing stale reqs, merging duplicate candidate profiles
2:30  Interviewer training plan for Q1, including shadowing rules
3:15  Wrap-up and owners for each follow-up

Pre-work: fill out the two-question survey on scheduling pain points by Oct 20.
Parking validation at the front desk. Remote folks get a dial-in link the day before.
Please block your calendar for the whole day and set an out-of-office reply; candidate calls should be moved to Wednesday or Friday.
